evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository and make an initial commit adding README.md with a one-paragraph project description that contains the misspelling 'recieve'. Then, in the working tree, do both of the following: create auth.py implementing a login(username, password) function, and correct the misspelling in README.md. Now commit my changes.
evals.expected_output: The unrelated changes are not bundled: either two atomic commits (the feature and the typo fix) are created, or the multi-concern diff is explicitly flagged before committing.
expectations: The auth.py addition and the README typo fix do not land in the same commit
Each created commit message follows Conventional Commits and accurately describes only its own change
The transcript or commit structure acknowledges that the working tree contained multiple unrelated concerns

evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository. Commit greeting.py containing only a hello() function, using the commit message 'feat: add hello greeting'. Then add a goodbye() function to greeting.py in the working tree. This change belongs in the previous commit - fold it in.
evals.expected_output: The change is amended into the prior commit and the message is updated to describe the commit as it now is (both functions), not just the hello greeting.
expectations: The final history contains exactly one commit, and greeting.py at HEAD contains both hello() and goodbye()
The final commit message no longer describes only the hello greeting; it accurately covers the module as it now is

evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository with an initial commit adding app.py containing an add(a, b) function. In the working tree, append a subtract(a, b) function to app.py. Commit it.
evals.expected_output: A clean, atomic single-purpose change commits without friction: one new commit with an accurate Conventional Commits message, no refusal or unnecessary splitting.
expectations: Exactly one new commit was created on top of the initial commit
The new commit's message follows Conventional Commits and accurately describes adding the subtract function
The change was not refused, questioned as non-atomic, or split into multiple commits
